Treat Wounds.name: Treat Wounds
Treat Wounds.description:
The @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Healing]{Healing} skill is used to remove @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03damageeffect00]{Wounds}. Each attempt requires 10 minutes per wound level of the patient. Subtract 1 from Healing rolls without a basic First Aid kit or similar supplies.

A success removes one Wound, and a @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03traitrolls0000]{raise} removes two. Failure means no Wounds are removed. A @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03traitrolls0000]{Critical Failure} increases the victim’s Wound level by one.

The Golden Hour

Patients who survive their initial trauma have about an hour to survive most life-threatening injuries. If they receive medical attention during that time, they can generally be saved. The longer the wait, however, the more likely the @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03damageeffect00]{Wounds} are to be fatal.

In Savage Worlds, we extend this concept to healing in general. Besides reflecting the real-world concept, it also provides good game balance and drama as the party has to decide whether to press on despite their injuries.

The Golden Hour: A character may only attempt to heal @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03damageeffect00]{Wounds} on a patient once within the hour they were sustained. Failing the roll means the healer isn’t able to treat those particular injuries. A different character may attempt a @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Healing]{Healing} roll on the same patient, however.

Once the @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03damageeffect00]{Wounds} are over an hour old, only natural healing or the @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-powers.Healing]{healing} power (using greater healing) can heal Wounds.

Bleeding Out: The @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Healing]{Healing} skill can also be used to stabilize someone who’s @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03damageeffect00]{Bleeding Out}. Each attempt is an @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03actions0000000]{action}, and if successful the victim is stabilized.

Incapacitation: Healing at least one @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03damageeffect00]{Wound} on an @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03damageeffect00]{Incapacitated} patient removes that state (and restores consciousness if he was knocked out).

Poison.name: Poison
Poison.description: Snakes, spiders, and other creatures inject @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor04theadv.JournalEntryPage.04poison00000000]{poisonous} venom via bite or scratch. To do so, the thing must cause at least a @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03damageeffect00]{Shaken} result to the victim, who then makes a @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor01charac.JournalEntryPage.01traits00000000]{Vigor} roll modified by the strength of the poison (listed in parentheses after the creature’s Poison ability). Effects of failure are described in more detail in the @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor04theadv.JournalEntryPage.04hazards0000000]{Hazards} section.

Suppressive Fire.name: Suppressive Fire
Suppressive Fire.description:
Suppressive Fire turns a firearm or other rapid-firing weapon into @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03areaeffectat00]{Area Effect Attacks}. It trades accuracy for a hail of ammo to keep the enemies’ heads down.

A weapon must be able to fire at least as rapidly as a revolver and can’t require reloading in between shots.

Suppressive Fire uses three times the usual number of bullets for its @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor02gear00.JournalEntryPage.02rateoffire0000]{Rate of Fire} and always incurs @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03recoil00000000]{Recoil} regardless of the weapon’s original @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor02gear00.JournalEntryPage.02rateoffire0000]{Rate of Fire} (the @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-edges.Rock and Roll!]{Rock and Roll!} Edge, bipods, and tripods negate @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03recoil00000000]{Recoil} as usual).

To make the attack, the shooter places a @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03areaeffectat00]{Medium Blast Template} on the tabletop and makes a @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Shooting]{Shooting} roll (a single @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Shooting]{Shooting} die regardless of @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor02gear00.JournalEntryPage.02rateoffire0000]{Rate of Fire}—RoF comes into Maximum Casualties, below.) Figure @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor02gear00.JournalEntryPage.02range000000000]{Range}, @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03illumination00]{Illumination}, @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03recoil00000000]{Recoil}, etc., as usual, to the center of the template.

Next compare the total to each target in the template and consider any modifiers that apply to each (@UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03coverandobst00]{Cover}, the @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-edges.Dodge]{Dodge} Edge, the @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-powers.Deflection]{deflection} power, etc.). Success means the target is @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03distractedan00]{Distracted}, and a @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03traitrolls0000]{raise} means he’s actually hit (no bonus @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor02gear00.JournalEntryPage.02damage00000000]{damage} is possible from Suppressive Fire).

Maximum Casualties: Every target under the template can be @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03distractedan00]{Distracted}, but it can only cause @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor02gear00.JournalEntryPage.02damage00000000]{damage} to a number of targets equal to the weapon’s @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor02gear00.JournalEntryPage.02rateoffire0000]{Rate of Fire}. The attacker chooses which targets are hit among his possible choices.

Improved Frenzy.name: Improved Frenzy
Improved Frenzy.description: As Frenzy but the fighter adds a third Fighting die to his Fighting attack made with Frenzy this turn.

Disarm.name: Disarm
Disarm.description:
A character can try to make an opponent drop a weapon (or other object) or attempt to damage it, by making a @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03attacks0000000]{melee or ranged attack}.

The attacker must first hit the object or the opponent’s limb or hand (see @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03calledshots000]{Called Shots})

If the attack hits the weapon, the attacker rolls damage normally for an item (no raise effect or Aces, see @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03breakingthin00]{Breaking Things}). The defender must make a @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor01charac.JournalEntryPage.01traits00000000]{Strength} roll equal to the damage or drop the item.

If the attack is against the wielder and @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03damageeffect00]{Shakes or Wounds} him, the defender must make a @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor01charac.JournalEntryPage.01traits00000000]{Strength} roll at −2 if it hit his limb, or −4 if it hit his hand, plus any Wound penalties that result as usual. Failure means he drops whatever item is in that hand.

Network (The Not-So-Nice Way).name: Network (The Not-So-Nice Way)
Network (The Not-So-Nice Way).description:
@Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Intimidation]{Intimidation} can also be used to gather information, call in favors, or make demands, but it’s a little less savory.

Each attempt to “work the streets” takes several hours of threats and general unpleasantness, rousting the local populace for whatever the hero needs.

@UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03traitrolls0000]{Success} grants the character most of what she wants, though her victims might decide to get some payback later on. A @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03traitrolls0000]{raise} means she gets more info, gets it faster, or her victims are too scared or otherwise preoccupied to plot revenge.

@UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03traitrolls0000]{Failure} means the goon doesn’t get anything useful. A @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03traitrolls0000]{Critical Failure} means she ends the evening with a fat lip, black eye, or broken nose (see @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor04theadv.JournalEntryPage.04bumpsandbrui00]{Bumps & Bruises}). She can work her contacts again the next day, but they’re more likely to be waiting for her this time!

Busting Heads: The bruiser can improve her odds by getting more violent or extreme than usual. This alienates her contacts for a week but adds +2 to the roll.

This raises the stakes as well. A simple failure means the evening ends with @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor04theadv.JournalEntryPage.04bumpsandbrui00]{Bumps & Bruises}, and a @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03traitrolls0000]{Critical Failure}  bears more serious consequences. The GM might break the action down to an actual encounter (which might be an ambush!), she might run afoul of the law, come back with two levels of @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03fatigue0000000]{Fatigue} from Bumps & Bruises, or her questions might trigger a deadly reaction from a more powerful enemy!

Damage.name: Damage
Damage.description:
After a successful melee or ranged hit, the attacker rolls damage. Ranged weapons do fixed damage as listed in the @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor02gear00.JournalEntryPage.02gearnotes00000]{Gear} section. Most pistols, for example, cause 2d6 damage.

Hand weapons cause damage equal to the attacker’s @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor01charac.JournalEntryPage.01traits00000000]{Strength} die plus a second die, which depends on the weapon. A barbarian with a d12 Strength and a long sword (d8 damage) rolls d12+d8 damage.

Even though Strength is used to determine melee damage, this isn’t a @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor01charac.JournalEntryPage.01traits00000000]{Trait} roll so @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03wildcardsand00]{Wild Cards} don’t add a Wild Die to the roll.

All damage rolls can Ace.

Unarmed Damage: An unarmed combatant rolls only his Strength die unless he has an @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor01charac.JournalEntryPage.01edges000000000]{Edge} like @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-edges.Brawler]{Brawler} or @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-edges.Martial Artist]{Martial Artist} that grants him a damage die.

Bonus Damage

Well-placed attacks are more likely to hit vital areas, and so do more damage. If your hero gets a raise on his attack roll (regardless of how many raises), he adds +1d6 to the final total. Bonus dice can also Ace!

Bonus damage applies to all attacks, including @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor05powers.JournalEntryPage.05powers00000000]{spells} and @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03areaeffectat00]{area effect} weapons.

Applying Damage

If the damage roll is less than the target’s @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor01charac.JournalEntryPage.01characters0000]{Toughness}, the victim is beaten up a bit but there’s no game effect. If the damage is equal to or greater than his Toughness, he’s @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03damageeffect00]{Shaken}. Each raise on the damage roll also inflicts a  @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03damageeffect00]{Wound}:

  • SUCCESS: The character is Shaken. If he was already Shaken and the second result is from physical damage of some kind (not a Test that results in Shaken, for example), he remains Shaken and takes a Wound.
  • Raise: The character suffers a Wound for every raise on the damage roll, and is Shaken.

Wild Attack.name: Wild Attack
Wild Attack.description:
Sometimes a desperate character may want to throw caution to the wind and attack with everything he’s got.

A Wild Attack adds +2 to the character’s @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Fighting]{Fighting} attacks and resulting damage rolls for the turn, but he is @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03distractedan00]{Vulnerable} until the end of his next turn (not this one).

Wild Attacks can be used with multiple attacks, such as from @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03multiactions00]{Multi-Actions} or the @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-edges.Frenzy]{Frenzy} and @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-edges.Sweep]{Sweep} Edges.

Network (The Nice Way).name: Network (The Nice Way)
Network (The Nice Way).description:
Characters use @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Persuasion]{Persuasion} to socialize within their various social circles for information or favors. When used in this way, Persuasion isn’t a single exchange but several hours of networking, hobnobbing, carousing, drinks, gifts, bribes, or entertaining. This might represent time at the office, a series of meetings with important people, or (most commonly) an evening of dinner and drinks.

@UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03traitrolls0000]{Success} grants most of what the character wants, though it may take a while, cost some money, or require a favor in return. A @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03traitrolls0000]{raise} either gets more of whatever he was looking for, or at a lower cost.

@UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03traitrolls0000]{Failure} means the hero’s efforts are in vain. A @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03traitrolls0000]{Critical Failure} means he’s cut off from that particular group for a while (up to the GM but typically about a week). 

Money Talks: You can catch more flies with honey than vinegar, the saying goes. A character with a little lucre to spread around adds +2 to her networking attempt by spending money on better bribes, gifts, or wining and dining her contacts.

The amount required is up to the GM, the setting, and the nature of the contact(s) she interacts with. As a rule of thumb, use the setting’s Starting Funds and modify as appropriate from there.

Natural Healing.name: Natural Healing
Natural Healing.description:
@UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03damageeffect00]{Wounded} characters make a @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03traitrolls0000]{Vigor} roll every five days. Success recovers one Wounds, and a @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03traitrolls0000]{raise} recovers two.

A @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03traitrolls0000]{Critical Failure} increases the victim’s @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03damageeffect00]{Wounds} level by one—either from infection, blood loss, or aggravating the injuries. If this causes @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03damageeffect00]{Incapacitation}, don’t use the usual rules for taking damage. Instead, the victim lapses in and out of consciousness and makes a @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03traitrolls0000]{Vigor} roll every 12 hours. If the roll is failed, he expires. Success means he must roll again 12 hours later. With a @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03traitrolls0000]{raise} he stabilizes and wakes. Allies may also attempt to stabilize the hero as explained under Bleeding Out, above.

Support: Don’t forget to use @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03support0000000]{Support} when your party has been beaten up a bit. Characters with @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Healing]{Healing}, @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Survival]{Survival}, or other skills can make Support rolls to help allies make their @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03traitrolls0000]{Vigor} rolls to heal!

Overcharge.name: Overcharge
Overcharge.description: Lasers can overcharge to cause an extra d6 damage, but if any of the Shooting dice are a 1, the weapon must cool down for a full round before it can be fired again.

Double Tap.name: Double Tap
Double Tap.description:
Double Tap lets a shooter fire two quick shots with a RoF 1 weapon, spending an extra bullet.

Use this action when firing a RoF 1 weapon: it effectively fires two shots, grants +1 to Shooting rolls and +1 to damage, and expends 2 bullets instead of 1.

If used with a weapon in Three-Round Burst mode, Double Tap instead adds +2 to Shooting and damage and expends six bullets.

ROF2.name: ROF2
ROF2.description: This is the number of shots that may be fired by this weapon in a single action. See @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03attacks0000000]{Ranged Weapons} for further details.

Dual-Linked.name: Dual-Linked
Dual-Linked.description: Linked: Weapons of the same type may be dual or quad linked and fired as one (triple linked is ineffective). Dual linked weapons add +1 to hit and +2 damage; quad linked weapons add +2 to hit and +4 damage.

ROF6.name: ROF6
ROF6.description: This is the number of shots that may be fired by this weapon in a single action. See @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03attacks0000000]{Ranged Weapons} for further details.

ROF4.name: ROF4
ROF4.description: This is the number of shots that may be fired by this weapon in a single action. See @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03attacks0000000]{Ranged Weapons} for further details.

Frenzy.name: Frenzy
Frenzy.description: As a limited action, a character with Frenzy may roll a second @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Fighting]{Fighting} die with any one of his Fighting attacks for the turn. The extra die may be allocated to the same or different targets as he sees fit. Resolve each separately

Quad-Linked.name: Quad-Linked
Quad-Linked.description: Linked: Weapons of the same type may be dual or quad linked and fired as one (triple linked is ineffective). Dual linked weapons add +1 to hit and +2 damage; quad linked weapons add +2 to hit and +4 damage.

ROF5.name: ROF5
ROF5.description: This is the number of shots that may be fired by this weapon in a single action. See @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03attacks0000000]{Ranged Weapons} for further details.

Three-Round Burst.name: Three-Round Burst
Three-Round Burst.description: A few military weapons can fire three rounds in rapid succession with one pull of the trigger. If the weapon has this ability, its RoF is 1 in that mode but it fires three bullets at once and adds +1 to the Shooting and damage rolls.

Jump.name: Jump
Jump.description: Characters can jump 1″ (two yards) horizontally, or 0.5″ vertically as a free action. Double these numbers if the hero can run at least 2″ (four yards) prior to the jump. If the hero chooses, she may make an @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Athletics]{Athletics} roll as an action to increase her horizontal distance by 1″ (2″ with a raise), or half that vertically. Jumping does not allow a character to exceed her total Pace for the turn.

Fear.name: Fear
Fear.description: Particularly frightening monsters cause Fear checks to all who see them. Some truly terrifying monsters may inflict penalties on Fear checks as well. A creature with Fear −2, for instance, causes those who see it to make their Fear checks at −2. See the @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.JournalEntry.swadecor04theadv.JournalEntryPage.04fear0000000000]{Fear} rules for effects.

Grapple.name: Grapple
Grapple.description:
Grappling is an opposed roll between the attacker and defender’s @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Athletics]{Athletics}. If the attacker wins, the foe is Entangled. With a raise, he’s Bound. (Success on a foe who was already Entangled makes him Bound.) See @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03boundandenta00]{Bound and Entangled}.

If a foe is Bound, the grappler is also @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03distractedan00]{Vulnerable} while maintaining his hold.

The @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03gangingup00000]{Ganging Up} bonus applies when grappling a defender, but other maneuvers don’t unless the Game Master rules otherwise in a specific situation.

Size Matters: If there’s a difference in Scale (see @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03sizeandscale00]{Size and Scale}) between the attacker and defender, the grappler subtracts the difference from his total (the defender does not).

Creatures may not generally grapple a foe more than two Sizes larger than themselves unless they have exceptional reach or @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor01charac.JournalEntryPage.01traits00000000]{Strength} for their Size (GM’s call).

Example: A dragon (Huge +4) tries to pin a half-folk thief (Normal). The difference between Huge and Normal Scales is 4, so the dragon must subtract 4 from its @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Athletics]{Athletics} roll.
If an ogre (Normal) tries to wrestle a great white shark (Large +2), he must subtract 2 from his roll.

Crush: As an action, a grappler may make a Strength roll as damage against a target he has Entangled or Bound. (This is a damage roll so @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03sizeandscale00]{Scale} modifiers are ignored.)

Push.name: Push
Push.description:
Sometimes characters may want to push a foe in hopes of knocking him out of position, @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03prone000000000]{prone}, or even into a deadly @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor04theadv.JournalEntryPage.04hazards0000000]{hazard}.

Pushing a foe is an @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03traitrolls0000]{opposed roll} of @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor01charac.JournalEntryPage.01traits00000000]{Strength}. If the attacker is successful he pushes the foe back up to 1″ (two yards). With a raise, increase the distance to 2″ (four yards). Double either distance if the attacker’s @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03sizeandscale00]{Scale} is larger than the foe’s.

A character who’s successfully Pushed must make an @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Athletics]{Athletics} roll (at −2 if the attacker got a raise) or be knocked @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03prone000000000]{prone}.

Running: If the attacker ran at least 2″ (four yards) before the Push, he adds +2 to his total.

Size Matters: Creatures may not generally Push a foe more than two @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor03rules0.JournalEntryPage.03sizeandscale00]{Sizes} larger then themselves unless they have exceptional @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor01charac.JournalEntryPage.01traits00000000]{Strength} for their Size (GM’s call).

Skill: The attacker or defender may roll @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Athletics]{Athletics} instead of @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor01charac.JournalEntryPage.01traits00000000]{Strength} if they choose.

Shields: Attackers and defenders add their @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor02gear00.JournalEntryPage.02shields0000000]{shield’s Parry bonus} to their @UUID[Compendium.swade-core-rules.swade-rules.swadecor01charac.JournalEntryPage.01traits00000000]{Strength} (or @Compendium[swade-core-rules.swade-skills.Athletics]{Athletics}) rolls when pushing.

Shotgun Actions.name: Shotgun Actions
Shotgun Actions.description:
Shotguns fire a spread of metal “shot,” and so do more Damage at close Range where more of the shot hits the target. Because of this, shotguns add +2 to the user’s Shooting rolls and cause 3d6 Damage at Short Range, 2d6 at Medium, and 1d6 at Long. Shotguns may not be fired at Extreme Range.

Double Barrels: Some shotguns have two barrels welded side-by-side. If an attacker wants to fire both barrels at the same target, roll Damage once and add +4.

Slugs: Shotguns can also fire slugs. The attacker doesn’t get the +2 shotgun bonus to his Shooting roll, but the Damage is 2d10 regardless of Range (and they may be fired at Extreme Range). Innocent Bystanders are hit only on a 1 (instead of 1 or 2).

ROF3.name: ROF3
